reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Scoring an epidural mass as 1 (it scores 0).
name: Rotterdam CT Score

version.label: Rotterdam CT score (Maas et al. 2005)
version.detail: Four items plus 1, giving 1–6. Mortality figures are 6-month mortality in adults with moderate or severe TBI in the derivation data.

purpose: CT-based prognostic score in traumatic brain injury.
intendedPopulation: Adults with moderate or severe traumatic brain injury.

inputDefinitions.label: Epidural mass lesion
inputDefinitions.help: Note the direction: an epidural mass scores 0 and its absence scores 1.

resultStates.label: Score 1
resultStates.summary: Rotterdam 1 at this assessment: 0% 6-month mortality in the derivation data.
resultStates.detail: Group-level figure for adults with moderate or severe TBI.

resultStates.label: Score 5
resultStates.detail: Group-level figure; integrate with clinical findings.

resultStates.label: Score 6
resultStates.detail: Group-level figure; integrate with clinical findings and avoid decisions on the score alone.

clinicalContext.text: Combines individual CT predictors and may discriminate better than the Marshall classification.

clinicalInsights.text: Paediatric mortality patterns differ from the adult figures shown.

limitations.text: Mortality figures apply to adults with moderate or severe TBI; mild TBI was not included.

limitations: Excludes contusions and subdural lesions as specific items.

guideSections.what: A 1–6 CT score from cisterns, shift, epidural mass and IVH/tSAH.
guideSections.whenToUse: Admission CT in moderate or severe TBI.
guideSections.howToPerform: Score the four items, sum and add 1.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A prognostic model input, not an individual prediction.

sources.citation: Maas AIR, Hukkelhoven CWPM, Marshall LF, Steyerberg EW. Prediction of outcome in traumatic brain injury with computed tomographic characteristics: a comparison between the computed tomographic classification and combinations of computed tomographic predictors. Neurosurgery. 2005;57(6):1173-1182.
